To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FlhAC is required for flagellar protein export and that FlhA(G368)C mutation causes the protease sensitivity of FlhAC.
the C-terminal domain of FlhAC is required for flagellar protein translocation into the growing flagellar rod structure.

FlhA and its C-terminal cytoplamsic domain (FlhAC), which is required for protein translocation by the bacterial flagellar protein export system, is involved in both docking and translocation of export substrates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of the flagellar type three protein translocation apparatus.
the molecular mechanism of protein export by the bacterial flagellae.
the role of the C-terminal cytosolic domain of FlhAC in flagellar protein export.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the G368C mutant of FlhA is defective in protein export, because the FliH, the FliI, the FliJ, or the export substrate cannot bind to the FlhAC of the FlhA(G368)C protein, and this is the reason for the temperature sensitivity.
FlhAC is required for the export of proteins through the flagellar type-III secretion machinery.
FlhAC plays a dual role in the flagellar type three protein export.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C-terminal cytosolic domain of FlhAC is required for protein translocation into the central channel.

the FlhA C-terminal cytoplamic domain is required to maintain the conformation of the FliH, FlhB C-terminal cytoplasic domain and FliH-FilI-FliJ export substrate complex to promote translocation of export substrates into the central channel.
the FlhAC domain of Flh A has two roles in the export process, one is the docking platform for FliH-FilI-FliJ and the other is the translocation gate for the substrate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a novel role of FlhAC in flagellar type III export.
we have identified the first intragenic suppressor mutation of the flhA gene, which has been shown to be essential for flagellar type III export.
FlhAC plays a role in flagellar type III secretion that is distinct from its role in docking of the export apparatus components.
